newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia to rebury slain presidents Tolbert, Doe.
newsitem.headline: Liberia to rebury slain presidents Tolbert, Doe.

text.p: Liberia's new president Charles Taylor has ordered that the remains of two slain predecessors be exhumed and given proper state burial, state radio reported on Sunday.
Taylor said an honourable burial for late presidents William Tolbert and Samuel Doe would be part of Liberia's healing process after a traumatic seven-year civil war.
"This is how we intend to begin the process of bringing our people back together," Taylor said in a briefing to reporters on Saturday broadcast by the radio.

"We have said August is the month of reconciliation and we mean business," added Taylor, a former warlord who won an emphatic mandate last month in presidential elections wrapping up civil war peace accords.
Taylor said he had invited international experts to help identify the bodies of the two men. He gave no dates.
Tolbert was killed in a military coup on August 12, 1980, led by Doe. Tolbert's body was dumped in a mass grave along with those of 13 senior aides, who were executed in public.
The coup ended the virtual dynasty of the descendants of freed American slaves who founded Liberia in 1847.
Doe himself was captured by rivals at the height of the civil war and tortured to death on September 10, 1990.
His body was buried in a shallow grave on a former rebel base on the outskirts of Monrovia but was exhumed and interred by his widow, Nancy, three years later.

Taylor started the war in December 1989. But Liberians looking for strong leadership after the conflict that killed well over 150,000 people voted massively for him and his National Patriotic Party in the July 19 elections.
